business_problem: EnergyAustralia needed to modernize its trading data stack for Australia's five-minute wholesale settlement cycle, volatile prices and higher-frequency battery and sensor data. Legacy delivery bottlenecks slowed pricing and forecasting updates, increasing the risk of pricing inaccuracies, weaker forecasts and greater financial exposure.
solution_summary: EnergyAustralia uses Databricks as part of its modernized Trading-domain data foundation. Five-minute settlement feeds, battery telemetry and generation inputs are brought together in one place so pricing, hedging and forecasting teams can work on trusted data instead of waiting hours for batch analytics. Business users write SQL and Python directly, build and test pricing methodologies, and push updates to production with Data Office support. Databricks Apps and native dashboards keep models, business logic and user-facing workflows in the same environment, while Unity Catalog supports the governance and quality controls needed for a federated operating model. The same platform also exposes detailed cost visibility by lab, workload, user and query so teams can tune long-running compute and scale self-service access refreshed every five minutes.

data_flow: Five-minute settlement feeds, battery telemetry and generation inputs land in Databricks, where trading teams use SQL and Python to update pricing, hedging and forecasting logic. Those outputs are delivered through Databricks Apps and native dashboards to business users, while Unity Catalog-backed governance and query-level cost visibility keep the environment controlled as access expands.
business_outcome: EnergyAustralia can work with near-real-time market data, deliver major initiatives 75% faster, refresh pricing curves hourly instead of daily and let most business users in Trading build directly in the platform while maintaining tighter cost and governance controls.
